title: File four numbered pages in order in a tray, laying pages aside until their turn
instruction: File the four numbered pages in the tray in order: page 4 at the bottom, then 3, then 2, with page 1 on top, each lying flat. The pages are in a mixed pile on the shelf, and you can lay pages on the shelf while you sort them.
context: Putting loose pages into numerical order is everyday clerical work: O*NET lists "Compile, copy, sort, and file records of office activities, business transactions, and other activities" for Office Clerks, General (43-9061.00, about 2.6 million US workers). Only the top page of a pile can be taken, so pages that come up too early have to be laid out on the desk and fetched when their turn comes, as a person does when collating. A page is 0.5 mm thick and lies flat, so a parallel gripper cannot lift it from above: it has to be pinched by an edge that sticks out, set down so that an edge still sticks out for the second pick, and filed flat on the pages already in the tray. Dumping the pile into the tray scores 0.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of a table. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table: x straight out, y to the left; heights above the table. Shelf: a black box 49.6 cm long (x 11.6 to 61.2), 20 cm deep (y 7.75 to 27.75) and 15 cm tall, fixed to the table, with a slick top (PTFE film or polished laminate; card slides on it at a friction coefficient of about 0.16). Pages: four A6 sheets of white 400 gsm card (14.8 x 10.5 cm, 0.5 mm thick, 6.2 g each), long side along x, each printed on its top face with one black numeral, 1, 2, 3 or 4, 9 cm tall and up to 5 cm wide with strokes 1.2 cm wide, its top toward the far end of the table. Pile: the four pages lie at the shelf's near end, centred at x 20.0. The pile is sheared: the top page's right edge is at y 5.95, 1.8 cm past the shelf's right edge (y 7.75), and each page below lies 1.8 cm further left (right edges at y 7.75, 9.55 and 11.35). Numbers from the top: 2, 4, 1, 3. The rest of the shelf's top, from x 28 to x 61, is free. Tray: on the table below the pile, against the shelf's right face, one open tray 16 cm long (x 12.0 to 28.0) and 17 cm deep (y -9.45 to 7.55) inside: a grey floor 4 mm thick and three dark grey walls 4 mm thick whose tops are 2.5 cm above the table; the shelf's face is its fourth side. Tray: smooth plastic or laminated board, fixed to the table. A second pile order is provided for a second layout, from the top: 3, 1, 4, 2.
scoring: Measured at the end of the trial. A page counts as in the tray when it lies flat there: seen from above, all of it is inside the tray (from the shelf's face to the outside of the walls, within 2 mm); it is tilted at most 10 degrees (one edge at most 1.8 cm higher than the opposite edge); and its lowest point is within 6 mm of the tray's floor. A page leaning on a wall or held above the tray does not count. Take the pages in the tray off one at a time from the top and read them back from the bottom up. Count how many, starting from the bottom page, match the wanted order 4, 3, 2, 1; stop at the first that does not. Score = (pages in order minus the other pages in the tray) / 4, never below 0: 0.25 for page 4 at the bottom, 0.5 with page 3 on it, 0.75 with page 2, 1.0 with page 1 on top, and each page in the tray out of order cancels one. Pages left on the shelf, on the table or off the table add and subtract nothing. 1.0 (success, which ends the trial): all four pages in the tray in order and still (moving under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. Dumping the pile into the tray leaves pages out of order and scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Take the four pages out of the tray and rebuild the pile at the shelf's near end in the listed order, numerals up with their tops toward the far end of the table, each page 1.8 cm to the right of the one below and the top page's edge 1.8 cm past the shelf's edge. Wipe the shelf's top if it has picked up dust.
fidelity: Each page is a rigid plate the size and weight of A6 400 gsm card; it does not bend, crease or flutter (air drag is modelled as damping). The numerals are drawn on the top face only and are not felt. Friction: card on card 0.30 static and 0.25 kinetic, card on the shelf's top 0.16 and 0.135, finger pad on card 0.40 and 0.375. The shelf and tray are fixed. Card is used because thin office paper is too floppy to model as a rigid plate.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; both arms reached toward the pile and the tray again and again, but no page was taken and the pile stayed on the shelf); demo: 1.0 (success at step 1,307)
